dv360.shortDescription: Programmatic advertising through Google Display & Video 360.
dv360.description: DV360 is Google's demand-side platform for programmatic advertising. It offers access to premium inventory and advanced targeting at scale.
dv360.useCase: Programmatic display and video advertising at scale.
dv360.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI deploys DV360 as part of larger media strategies. We make sure programmatic campaigns are properly connected to your tracking and that results are included in your overall reporting.
problemsSolved: Programmatic campaigns run apart from performance channels
No integrated overview of all media channels
dv360.stevinAngle: DV360 is Google's heavy programmatic platform: access to premium inventory and advanced targeting at scale, for display and video. It is powerful, but it is built for media teams and agencies, not for someone who just wants to run a campaign on the side. The trap is that programmatic at scale easily ends up in a silo: lots of impressions, lots of reach, but disconnected from what your performance channels actually bring in. We see advertisers stall on this: DV360 delivers volume, but there is no integrated picture where display and video sit next to search and social, so it stays unclear what the spend genuinely adds. Stevin runs as a layer on top, reads the campaign data through the API and puts it in your total reporting, with an eye on whether the tracking carries through correctly. A person sees the conclusion first, then comes a budget decision.
dv360.stackImpact: Choosing DV360 means you are running programmatic at agency level, and that requires a correct tracking setup and a place where the results come together with your other channels. Without that connection it becomes volume without context. The data is available through the API, so that is not the problem. The real question is whether display and video are measurable next to search and social, or whether they stay a separate silo. Without that integrated picture you steer on impressions instead of on contribution.
pitfalls: Letting programmatic run in a silo, apart from your performance channels.
Steering on impressions and reach because the contribution does not sit next to other channels.
Not checking the tracking setup, so conversions carry through wrong or not at all.
Assuming scale is the same as value without an integrated overview.

facebook-graph.shortDescription: Facebook Page insights, post engagement, and community management.
facebook-graph.description: Facebook Pages remain an important channel for communities, events, and direct communication with fans. The Graph API offers access to page-level metrics and post performance.
facebook-graph.useCase: Monitoring page performance and tracking community engagement.
facebook-graph.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI syncs your Facebook Page data and combines it with Instagram and other channels for a cross-platform overview of your organic reach.
problemsSolved: Facebook data sits apart from your other social channels
Post engagement is not analyzed systematically
facebook-graph.stevinAngle: Facebook Pages get written off a lot, but for communities, events, and direct communication with a slightly older audience they still do work. The Graph API opens up the page level: post performance, engagement, the usual metrics. What the API does not do is bring your Facebook data into context with the rest. It stays an island, apart from your Instagram, apart from your other channels, even though it is often the same audience doing something in two places. Teams get stuck on that double picture: two tabs, two stories, no overview. Stevin reads the Facebook Page data through the Graph API and lines it up against your other sources, so a trend in engagement or a post that takes off surfaces as a signal instead of sitting in a loose dashboard. You set the follow-up, the person reviews it.
facebook-graph.stackImpact: Facebook Page data comes through the same Graph infrastructure as Instagram, so if you already have that set up this channel costs little on top. The bottleneck is not the connection but the coherence: Facebook and Instagram often share an audience, and if you read them separately your picture drifts apart. So you need something that lines the channels up side by side instead of two loose reports. Skip that, and you are paying attention to a channel you cannot tie to the rest anyway, and Facebook stays an island.
pitfalls: Reporting Facebook and Instagram separately, so the same audience is counted twice or inconsistently.
Writing the channel off and missing events and community signals from an older audience.
Collecting page data without anything that pulls trends out, so it becomes a dead dashboard.

google-ads.shortDescription: Advertising on Google Search, Display, Shopping and YouTube.
google-ads.description: Google Ads is the largest advertising platform in the world. From search ads to shopping and display, it gives you direct access to buying intent. But without solid tracking, landing pages and follow-up, it is also a platform where budget leaks away fast.
google-ads.useCase: Generate leads and customers through search intent, remarketing and shopping campaigns.
google-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Google Ads to your CRM, tracking and automation. We make sure conversions are measured correctly, that leads are picked up automatically, and that your campaigns are optimized on real customer value, not just clicks.
problemsSolved: Conversions are not measured correctly
Leads from Google Ads are not followed up fast enough
No insight into which campaigns genuinely produce customers
Budget leaks away through poor connection with the rest of the funnel
google-ads.stevinAngle: In 80 percent of the accounts we take over, Google Ads is not broken, it is read wrong. The dashboard shows conversions that Google did not cause: branded search that would have happened anyway, retargeting of warm traffic, comparison sites that had already secured the purchase. We run a geo test or holdout by default within the first month, to measure what actually comes in on top versus what would have converted without Google Ads anyway. The numbers from a test like that are structurally 20 to 40 percent off from what the Google dashboard reports itself.
google-ads.stackImpact: For your stack this means: tie Google Ads to an external baseline (CRM, P&L or a holdout segment), not just to Google's own conversion API. We send leads server-side straight to your CRM with the Click ID, so you can trace per lead which keyword, which campaign and which ad produced it. After that we measure customer value out to 12 months past the first click. Only then do you see which campaigns genuinely produce customers instead of clicks.
pitfalls: Running Performance Max without excluding branded keywords, it catches demand that was already there but still costs budget
Leaving conversion modeling on without understanding that you are then counting model estimates, not measured conversions
Smart Bidding on conversion volumes that are too low (under 30 a month), the algorithm has too little signal and starts guessing
No frequency cap on display, so a user gets served 40 times for one click

faqs.question: Does Stevin.AI also manage my Google Ads campaigns?
faqs.answer: Yes, we manage campaigns and make sure they are set up properly on the technical side, connected to your tracking and CRM, and optimised for real results.

faqs.question: Do you take a margin on my advertising budget?
faqs.answer: No. You pay your media budget straight to Google. We do not charge a margin or commission on your ad spend.

google-analytics-4.shortDescription: Website analytics and conversion tracking from Google.
google-analytics-4.description: Google Analytics 4 is the standard for website analytics. It gives insight into user behavior, traffic sources and conversions. But only if it is set up well, and at many companies that is not the case.
google-analytics-4.useCase: Measuring website traffic, conversions and user behavior.
google-analytics-4.howWeUseIt: Stevin sets up GA4 correctly: from enhanced measurement to custom events, conversion goals and connections to Google Ads. We make sure your data is reliable and that your reports line up with your commercial goals.
problemsSolved: GA4 is not configured well
Conversions are not measured correctly
No link between website data and campaign performance
Reports give no usable insight
google-analytics-4.stevinAngle: In most accounts GA4 is technically installed but fundamentally set up wrong. Default conversions usually do not count what you want to measure (for example 'Generate Lead' on a form submit, while your real conversion is a qualified lead in your CRM). Data sampling on large properties hides exactly the detail that is meaningful. We use GA4 as traffic-source reporting and behavioral analysis, not as the attribution source for budget decisions. For that last part we go to the CRM or an MMM.
google-analytics-4.stackImpact: Three technical things we fix as standard: server-side Google Tag Manager for tracking reliability (halving cookie loss of 20 to 40 percent), custom events that measure your funnel steps instead of Google's defaults, and a BigQuery connection so you can join GA4 data with CRM data. Only in BigQuery does GA4 become a real analysis tool instead of a dashboard.
pitfalls: Counting conversions on the pageview of the thank-you page when that page does not always load (SPAs, redirects)
Reading 'engaged sessions' as conversions: Google's definition is 10 seconds, which is not engagement
Cross-domain tracking not set up for your checkout on a different subdomain, splitting sessions
Leaving data retention on the default 2 months when you need 14 months for year-over-year comparisons

faqs.question: Can Stevin.AI improve my existing GA4?
faqs.answer: Yes. We audit your current setup, fix errors, and rebuild events and conversions so your data becomes reliable.

google-merchant-center.shortDescription: Product data for Google Shopping, Free Listings, and Performance Max.
google-merchant-center.description: Google Merchant Center is the heart of your Google Shopping strategy. Product titles, descriptions, prices, and availability determine how and whether your products appear in Shopping results.
google-merchant-center.useCase: Google Shopping feed management, product data quality, and free listings optimization.
google-merchant-center.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI monitors your Merchant Center for disapprovals, data quality issues, and performance per product group. Feed problems get flagged right away before they affect your campaigns.
problemsSolved: Product disapprovals get discovered too late
Feed data quality is inconsistent
No view of which product groups deliver the most
google-merchant-center.stevinAngle: Google Merchant Center is the heart of your Shopping presence: titles, prices, availability, and descriptions decide whether your products appear at all. Well filled, it is the quiet engine under your shopping revenue. The problem is that it stays quiet at the wrong moments. A disapproval, a data quality issue, or a product dropping out of view, you often notice only once sales drop, because Merchant Center does not actively push those signals to you. Teams get stuck there: the feed seems fine until a whole product group goes silent. Stevin monitors your Merchant Center for disapprovals, data quality, and performance per product group and turns a problem into a signal before it hits your campaigns. Not yet another email in a full inbox, but a targeted alert with what is going on. The consultant sees what needs attention and decides what gets fixed.
google-merchant-center.stackImpact: Choosing Merchant Center is not a choice if you want to be on Google Shopping, it is the foundation. But it is a data container, not a watchdog: it does not warn proactively when something goes wrong, and the alerts that exist drown in your inbox. Count on a layer that actively flags disapprovals and quality problems and links them to which product groups deliver the most, so attention goes to the right place. The data is in there, the attention is missing. Without something keeping watch, you discover a feed problem only once your revenue tells you, and by then you are already days behind.
pitfalls: Only discovering a disapproval once sales are already dropping.
Relying on a data container that does not warn proactively.
Letting data quality slide until a whole product group falls out of view.
Having no view of which product groups actually earn the budget.

google-search-console.shortDescription: Insight into your organic search performance in Google.
google-search-console.description: Google Search Console shows how your website performs in organic search results. From indexing to keywords and technical issues.
google-search-console.useCase: Monitoring organic search performance and technical SEO issues.
google-search-console.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Search Console data to identify SEO opportunities and optimize landing pages for both organic and paid traffic.
problemsSolved: No view of organic search performance
Technical SEO issues go undetected
google-search-console.stevinAngle: Google Search Console is the direct line to how Google sees your site: indexing, keywords and technical issues, straight from the source. It is free and indispensable, and that is also where the limit sits. Search Console shows it, but does nothing, and it keeps the data only briefly, so a trend or a sinking page easily slips away before anyone looks. We use it where it is strong: as a factual source on your organic performance. Where teams get stuck is that the data stays in the tool. A page that suddenly gets fewer impressions, a keyword that sinks, an indexing problem: it is in there, but nobody looks every day. That is where Stevin sits. As a layer on top of your stack, Stevin reads Search Console through the API and keeps the history, so that a meaningful drop or a new technical problem becomes a signal a person reviews, instead of something you only discover once the traffic is already gone.
google-search-console.stackImpact: Choosing Search Console costs nothing, but the data lives only briefly and the tool does nothing with what it shows. Count on wanting to hold the history somewhere, otherwise you miss trends because the window is too narrow. The data comes in through the API, so the real question is not whether you can access it, but whether someone watches the movements that matter. Without something that keeps the history and watches for deviations, Search Console stays a dashboard you open when it is already too late, not a source that warns you.
pitfalls: Relying on the short retention period, so trends slip away before you see them.
Leaving the data in the tool while nobody looks at it daily.
Only noticing a sinking page or indexing problem once the traffic is already gone.

google-sheets.shortDescription: Spreadsheets for data storage, reporting, and workflows.
google-sheets.description: Google Sheets is more than a spreadsheet. It is a flexible data hub you can connect to almost any marketing tool. Ideal for reporting, data enrichment, and as a middle layer in automations.
google-sheets.useCase: Flexible data storage and reporting as part of marketing workflows.
google-sheets.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Sheets as a link in automations: from lead lists to reporting exports and data enrichment via Zapier or Make.
problemsSolved: Data has to be moved between tools by hand
No central place for ad hoc reporting
google-sheets.stevinAngle: Google Sheets is much more than a spreadsheet. It is the flexible glue layer you connect to almost every marketing tool, ideal for lists, reporting exports, and enrichment. The strength is exactly that flexibility, you build something fast without heavy software. And that is where the risk sits too. A Sheet grows organically into a tab where nobody knows which formula depends on what, and data you type in by hand drifts away from your actual sources. We use it as a link in automations, not as a system of record. Where teams get stuck is that a Sheet becomes a quiet single point of failure: an import that stops or a cell that gets overwritten only shows up when a report comes out wrong. Stevin runs as a layer over your stack and uses Sheets as a waypoint, reads it through the API, and flags when data stops adding up or an expected update never lands, so a person steps in before it spreads.
google-sheets.stackImpact: Choosing Sheets as a link means you have something that ties almost everything together, but also something that can break quietly without anyone noticing. Treat it as a middle layer, not a source of truth, because manual entry drifts away from your real systems. The data is easy to read through the API, so the question is not whether you can get at it, but whether anyone notices when an import stalls or a cell gets overwritten. Without that check, a Sheet becomes a fragile heart of your workflow that nobody is watching.
pitfalls: Using a Sheet as a system of record, so data drifts away from your sources.
Letting formulas and links grow organically until nobody knows the dependencies anymore.
Catching a stopped import or an overwritten cell only when a report comes out wrong.

google-tag-manager.shortDescription: Tag management for handling tracking and pixels.
google-tag-manager.description: Google Tag Manager is the central point for all your tracking. Pixels, events, conversions: everything is managed through GTM. Set up well, it saves time and prevents errors. Set up badly, it causes data loss.
google-tag-manager.useCase: Central management of all tracking tags and marketing pixels.
google-tag-manager.howWeUseIt: Stevin sets up GTM according to best practices: clean containers, correct triggers, data layer implementation and server-side tagging where needed. We make sure all your tools receive reliable data.
problemsSolved: Tags fire incorrectly or twice
No overview in the GTM container
The data layer is not implemented or implemented badly
Server-side tagging is not set up
google-tag-manager.stevinAngle: GTM is not a marketing tool, it is tracking infrastructure. Most accounts treat it as 'the place where the marketer adds tags without a developer', which is technically true but leads to messy containers: 80 or more tags nobody can trace anymore, duplicate triggers, conflicting variables. We start every audit with a container clean: which tag is there and why, which still work, which pollute the signal. A clean container is a better ROI investment than a new campaign.
google-tag-manager.stackImpact: Server-side GTM is the standard in 2026, no longer optional. It solves three problems at once: data loss from browser restrictions (Safari ITP, ad blockers), latency on your site from fewer client-side scripts, and first-party data ownership instead of data that gets grabbed by 30 vendor pixels. We host server-side GTM on your own subdomain, not on Google's servers, so your data really sits in your stack.
pitfalls: Sticking with client-side GTM while your conversion match rate is already dropping below 60 percent
Using custom HTML tags for vendor pixels that do have a native template, more maintenance, no gain
Tying triggers to CSS classes the developer changes in a month, tracking quietly fails
Deploying a container without versioning or a preview-mode test, broken tracking goes live

instagram-graph-api.shortDescription: Organic Instagram metrics, comment monitoring, and engagement analysis.
instagram-graph-api.description: Instagram is the visual storefront for artists, brands, and creators. The Graph API gives access to reach, impressions, follower growth, and comment data at account and post level.
instagram-graph-api.useCase: Monitoring organic reach, filtering fan engagement, and sentiment analysis.
instagram-graph-api.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI pulls your Instagram metrics daily, filters high-intent comments out of the noise, and generates Advisor cards for engagement opportunities you would otherwise miss.
problemsSolved: Thousands of comments but no overview of what matters
Organic performance is not tied to ads strategy
No insight into follower growth trends per region
instagram-graph-api.stevinAngle: The Instagram Graph API gives you the numbers the app itself holds back: reach, impressions, follower growth, and every comment at post and account level. Solid and reliable, as long as you know it is raw data and not a judgment. That is exactly where the bottleneck sits. On an account with any volume, thousands of comments pour in, and most of them are noise. The one fan question that genuinely matters, a collaboration request, a complaint getting out of hand, disappears among the emoji. The API delivers everything, but filters nothing. Stevin runs as a work layer over the Graph API, pulls your metrics daily, and sifts the comments with intent from the rest. Whatever needs attention surfaces as a signal with a suggested reply, and you see it before anything goes out the door.
instagram-graph-api.stackImpact: Choosing the Graph API means setting up and maintaining a Meta app and the permissions that go with it, and Meta tightens the rules regularly. It gives you organic data, but it sits apart from your ads side, so for a complete picture you connect it to your advertising data. The comments arrive raw, with no filtering at all, so the value is in what happens on top. The real question is not whether you can get the metrics out, but whether something sifts the noise for you, because without that it stays a dashboard no one opens in time.
pitfalls: Underestimating permissions and app review, so the connection stalls on a Meta change.
Trying to read every comment by hand until it simply piles up untouched.
Looking at organic data apart from your ads data, so you miss half the story.

klaviyo.shortDescription: Email marketing and automation built specifically for e-commerce.
klaviyo.description: Klaviyo is the standard for e-commerce email marketing. Strong segmentation, automation, and native integrations with webshop platforms.
klaviyo.useCase: Advanced email marketing and automation for webshops.
klaviyo.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Klaviyo to your webshop, ads, and tracking so your flows and segments are fed the right data and stay relevant.
problemsSolved: Email flows are not aligned with how customers actually behave
Segmentation is too broad or not driven by data
klaviyo.stevinAngle: Klaviyo was built for e-commerce, and you feel it in every feature. For D2C brands on Shopify or WooCommerce, Klaviyo is the default, not because it has the prettiest UI but because the product-data hooks work out of the box: viewed product, added to cart, started checkout, all of it triggerable without a developer. For B2B or services, Klaviyo is overkill and you miss flow features that HubSpot or ActiveCampaign do have. So watch the hype: Klaviyo does not solve every email problem, it solves e-commerce email well.
klaviyo.stackImpact: Three flows every Klaviyo account should have before it thinks about campaigns: a welcome series (3 to 5 emails over the week after signup), abandoned cart (1 email within the hour, 1 within 24 hours), and post-purchase (a review request after 14 days, a cross-sell after 30 days). In our data these flows deliver 30 to 40 percent of total email revenue, while you build them once and they run on their own. Campaigns, segmentation, and SMS come after that, not before.
pitfalls: Turning on the SMS channel without a TCPA-compliant opt-in flow. US fines run into five figures.
Using predictive analytics on accounts under 10,000 customers. The model has too little data, so the predictions are noise.
Building segments on 'Active in last 30 days' without defining what 'active' means. The segment fills up with junk fast.
Pushing email frequency past 3 per week without unsubscribe triage. List churn speeds up and deliverability drops.

linkedin-ads.shortDescription: B2B advertising on LinkedIn for targeted lead generation.
linkedin-ads.description: LinkedIn Ads is the leading B2B advertising platform. The cost per click is higher, but the quality of leads is often better. That makes solid follow-up and tracking extra important.
linkedin-ads.useCase: B2B lead generation and account-based marketing through LinkedIn.
linkedin-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects LinkedIn Ads to your CRM and makes sure leads from LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms are synced automatically. We measure through to the customer level so you know which campaigns genuinely produce revenue.
problemsSolved: High cost per lead with no insight into quality
Lead Gen Forms are not connected to the CRM
No view of the ROI of LinkedIn campaigns
linkedin-ads.stevinAngle: LinkedIn Ads has the highest cost per click in the market and the best targeting by job title or company size, both are true. What most accounts miss: LinkedIn's attribution window is 30 days and B2B cycles are 3 to 9 months. A lead that comes in six weeks after the first impression through Google gets zero credit from LinkedIn but was activated by it. We do not measure LinkedIn on conversions within 30 days, we measure on pipeline influence across the whole deal cycle.
linkedin-ads.stackImpact: For B2B this means: connect LinkedIn to your CRM at the company level (matched audiences, lead routing to BDRs, opportunity tagging). Only then do you see that a LinkedIn touchpoint is often not the 'last click' but the 'first touch' that made the whole deal possible. Combine it with Bombora or 6sense for intent data so you know when a target account is actively in-market.
pitfalls: Measuring ROAS over a 30-day window while your sales cycle is 6 months
Using Lead Gen Forms without an enrichment step, you get name and email but no role or company size
Sending Sponsored InMail to cold traffic, opt-out rates of 80 percent and up, hurts your long-term match rate
Targeting by job title without a seniority filter, junior staff in the funnel who never decide

mailchimp.shortDescription: Email marketing and basic automation for SMBs.
mailchimp.description: Mailchimp is one of the best-known email marketing platforms. Easy to use, with options for newsletters, automations, and landing pages.
mailchimp.useCase: Email newsletters and basic automation for SMBs.
mailchimp.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Mailchimp to your CRM and lead sources so new leads land in the right list automatically and get the right follow-up flow.
problemsSolved: New leads are not added to email lists automatically
Email campaigns are not connected to CRM data
mailchimp.stevinAngle: In 2026 Mailchimp is a fine entry-level tool and a poor primary platform for growing companies. The line sits around 10,000 contacts or 50 euros a month: below that Mailchimp is cheap and simple, above it you pay for features you get for free elsewhere. We regularly migrate from Mailchimp to ActiveCampaign or Klaviyo when a client crosses that threshold, it takes a week of work and structurally saves hundreds a month plus opens up automation options Mailchimp does not offer.
mailchimp.stackImpact: For anyone who does stay on Mailchimp: use tags instead of lists (lists overlap, tags are flexible), switch on double opt-in by default despite it lowering your conversion rate (long-term deliverability matters more), and connect to your site through the native API instead of Zapier bridges (faster, more reliable, no rate limits). The API connection is free and most accounts do not use it.
pitfalls: Letting the audience counter climb without unsubscribing inactive contacts, you pay for an empty list
Duplicating templates over and over instead of one template plus content blocks, maintenance becomes brand-inconsistent
Building automations that sit in series instead of as trigger-based workflows, mistimed sends
No sending-domain authentication (DKIM/SPF/DMARC), emails land in spam despite good content

meta-ads.shortDescription: Advertising on Facebook and Instagram for reach and lead generation.
meta-ads.description: Meta Ads gives you access to Facebook and Instagram. Ideal for reach, retargeting and lead generation. The strength is in the targeting and the volume, but without solid tracking and follow-up you cannot see what it produces.
meta-ads.useCase: Lead generation, retargeting and brand awareness through social advertising.
meta-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Meta Ads to your CRM and automation. We implement the Conversions API for reliable data delivery and make sure leads from lead forms land directly in your CRM with the right follow-up.
problemsSolved: Leads from lead forms are not picked up automatically
Conversion data is unreliable due to cookie loss
No link between ads and actual revenue
meta-ads.stevinAngle: Since iOS 14, Meta Ads has had a measurement problem that most accounts hide behind the Conversions API and advanced modeling. The reality: 30 to 50 percent of the conversions shown in Ads Manager are modeled, not measured. We implement the server-side Conversions API by default, but we only believe the number after an independent uplift measurement. On accounts where that has been done, Meta often turns out to be stronger on upper-funnel awareness and weaker on direct conversion than the dashboard suggests.
meta-ads.stackImpact: The Conversions API is no longer optional, it is the foundation. On top of that you tie lead forms straight to your CRM so the 24-hour follow-up starts automatically (Meta leads not called within 5 minutes convert 8x lower). For your reporting: separate 'Meta-attributed conversions' from 'CRM-attributed customers' in your dashboards. The gap between the two is your real work.
pitfalls: Using lead forms without a real-time webhook to the CRM, leads cool off sharply within an hour
Optimizing conversions on the 'Lead' event instead of on a qualified-lead event from your CRM
Building lookalike audiences on a seed list of fewer than 1000 customers, the model has too little signal
Running ASC (Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns) without checking whether it cannibalizes existing buyers

pinterest-ads.shortDescription: Visual advertising on Pinterest for inspiration and purchase.
pinterest-ads.description: Pinterest Ads targets users in the inspiration and planning phase. Ideal for e-commerce and brands with visual products. The intent is high, but tracking is essential to measure results.
pinterest-ads.useCase: Product discovery and conversions through visual advertising.
pinterest-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI integrates Pinterest with your webshop, tracking and product feeds. We make sure your Pinterest Tag is implemented correctly and that conversions are measured reliably.
problemsSolved: Product feeds are not connected properly
Conversion tracking is not set up properly
No insight into which pins convert
pinterest-ads.stevinAngle: Pinterest positions itself as the platform for the inspiration phase, but in practice we see at clients that the Pinterest Tag fires far too broadly by default. Without explicit deduplication against Google Analytics or your CDP, Pinterest records conversions that have already been credited elsewhere. The result is false confidence in your ROAS figures. What we do consistently in projects: configure the Tag with strict event-match quality, connect the API for Conversions alongside the browser tag, and reconcile both signals in your reporting layer. Only then do you see the real picture. For e-commerce clients with an average order value above 60 euros, Pinterest is worth serious consideration as a discovery channel, but only if your product feed is synced daily and your conversion windows are in line with your other platforms. Without that foundation you are measuring noise.
pinterest-ads.stackImpact: Pinterest Ads only works well once you have a reliable product feed pipeline, ideally through a feed management tool like Channable or DataFeedWatch that pushes to the Pinterest Catalog daily. On top of that you need the Pinterest API for Conversions as a server-side addition to the browser tag, which requires a backend connection to your webshop or order management system. If you want to take Pinterest data seriously in your attribution, your data pipeline to your BI tool or data warehouse has to include Pinterest as an explicit source, otherwise the channel disappears into the leftover category.
pitfalls: Installing the Pinterest Tag without event deduplication against your server-side connection leads to double-counted conversions and a ROAS that comes out structurally too high.
Uploading a product feed once without automatic syncing causes out-of-date prices and sold-out products in your ads, which hits your click-to-purchase ratio directly.
Conversion windows on Pinterest default to 30 days for clicks and 30 days for views, which with short funnels produces attribution that does not match how you measure your other channels.
Optimizing campaigns on Pinterest's own conversion reporting without mirroring it against your webshop data leads to budget choices based on figures you cannot trace internally.

shopify.description: Shopify is the most popular e-commerce platform for SMBs. User-friendly, scalable, and with extensive integration options.
shopify.useCase: Webshops connected to marketing and analytics.
shopify.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects your Shopify webshop to ads, tracking, email, and analytics. We make sure conversions are measured correctly, product feeds stay up to date, and customer data flows to your CRM.
problemsSolved: E-commerce tracking is not set up well
Product feeds are not synced with ad channels
Customer data does not reach the CRM
shopify.stevinAngle: For 80 percent of D2C brands in 2026, Shopify is the right platform. The remaining 20 percent sit in two groups: enterprise (choose Shopify Plus or another CMS), or niche (very specific checkout flows that Shopify does not support). We see teams that started on WooCommerce and migrate to Shopify because they no longer have time for WordPress maintenance. The other way around, we rarely see. The most important choices in a Shopify setup: themes ('Online Store 2.0' templates with sections), apps (as few as possible, every app slows your site down), and checkout customization (only really possible on Shopify Plus).
shopify.stackImpact: For your stack: Shopify integrates out of the box with most marketing tools (Klaviyo, Meta, Google), but watch out for apps that add their own scripts, that is how a Shopify site goes from 1.5s load time to 5s. Reviews, fulfillment, abandoned cart emails, all through a curated set of apps instead of 30 that overlap each other. For analytics: Shopify Analytics is fine as a baseline, but for real attribution connect to GA4 plus BigQuery plus Klaviyo.
pitfalls: Installing apps and never uninstalling them. Scripts keep loading even when you no longer use them.
Editing a theme without version control. The next theme update overwrites your work.
Using the standard checkout for B2B with separate VAT rules. It leads to wrong invoicing.
Not switching off Shopify Payments in markets where Mollie or Adyen converts better.

snapchat-ads.shortDescription: Advertising on Snapchat for younger audiences and AR formats.
snapchat-ads.description: Snapchat Ads gives access to a younger audience through Stories, Spotlight and AR Lenses. Strong for brands with visually strong creative and consumer-facing offerings.
snapchat-ads.useCase: Reach and conversion with younger audiences through vertical video and AR.
snapchat-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin implements the Snap Pixel and Conversions API and connects Snapchat to your tracking, CRM and MMM so you measure real incremental contribution.
problemsSolved: Conversion data is unreliable without a server-side connection
Snapchat's contribution is missing in the broader media mix
snapchat-ads.stevinAngle: Snapchat Ads brings you to a younger audience with Stories, Spotlight and AR Lenses, formats where visually strong brands make the difference. For consumer-facing offerings with good creative, that is the value: an audience you reach less easily on other platforms. We use it where that younger audience genuinely fits and the creative is in order. Where it pinches is measurement. Without a server-side connection through the Conversions API, the conversion data is unreliable, and without that, Snapchat's contribution gets lost in your broader mix. You see clicks, but not what they deliver. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and, once the Snap Pixel and CAPI are in place, reads the campaign data through the API next to your tracking and CRM. A lead that comes from Snapchat but does not get followed up, or spend that drifts away without return: that becomes a signal a person reviews, not a figure that without server-side measurement was already off.
snapchat-ads.stackImpact: Choosing Snapchat means the Snap Pixel and the Conversions API have to be set up seriously, otherwise you measure on sand. Count on a server-side connection as the first piece of work, because without it everything you report afterward is unreliable. The data comes in through the API, but the real condition is that the measurement is right before you place the contribution next to your other channels. Without that foundation, Snapchat stays a channel with nice clicks and an unknown return, and your picture drifts apart from what actually comes in.
pitfalls: Running Snapchat without server-side CAPI: the conversion data is then unreliable.
Deploying it without the creative in order, when the format leans entirely on that.
Reporting clicks without anyone checking whether a lead comes out that gets followed up.

tiktok-ads.shortDescription: Advertising on TikTok for reach among younger audiences.
tiktok-ads.description: TikTok Ads is growing fast as an advertising channel, especially for brands that want to reach younger audiences. The platform offers unique creative possibilities but demands solid tracking and measurability.
tiktok-ads.useCase: Brand awareness and conversions among younger audiences through short video ads.
tiktok-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements the TikTok Events API and connects the platform to your tracking and CRM. That way you measure not only views and clicks, but actual conversions and leads.
problemsSolved: Unreliable conversion data due to privacy restrictions
No connection to CRM or follow-up processes
Hard to measure ROI
tiktok-ads.stevinAngle: TikTok Ads works for the audiences where it works and not for the audiences where it does not. Sounds glib, but in practice it holds: for brands with an 18-34 audience it performs strongly on cost per acquisition, for B2B or 50-plus audiences it is symbolic. We see teams running TikTok because 'you are supposed to' without checking whether their audience is even there. The first step is always: measure whether your buyers are on it, not whether your competitors are advertising on it.
tiktok-ads.stackImpact: The Events API has to be on, otherwise you lose 40 percent of your conversion data to iOS and privacy restrictions. On top of that: TikTok creatives live 3 to 7 days before they hit creative fatigue. Plan a production cadence of at least 5 new creatives a week, otherwise your account goes into a downward spiral within a month. We feed creative performance back to the creative makers with automatic reports per asset.
pitfalls: Running an ad set until it stops working instead of 5 creatives in parallel with natural selection
Not using Spark Ads for creators you already follow organically, a missed lever
Optimizing web conversions in a market where 70 percent of your audience converts natively inside TikTok
Building lookalike audiences on all site traffic instead of on customers, the model gets the wrong signal

woocommerce.description: WooCommerce turns any WordPress site into a webshop. Flexible and open-source, with full control over your data.
woocommerce.useCase: E-commerce on WordPress with flexibility and control.
woocommerce.howWeUseIt: Stevin implements tracking, product feeds, and CRM connections for WooCommerce so your webshop is fully integrated with your marketing stack.
problemsSolved: WooCommerce data is not connected to marketing tools
E-commerce tracking is incomplete
woocommerce.stevinAngle: WooCommerce is not an e-commerce platform, it is a WordPress plugin that lets you do e-commerce. That distinction decides when to choose it and when not to. Do: when you already run WordPress for content marketing and the overlap is valuable. Do not: when you are purely transactional. Maintenance is structurally heavier than Shopify (security updates, plugin conflicts, hosting choices), costs look lower but add up. We migrate WooCommerce shops to Shopify on average 3 years after launch, when maintenance time no longer matches revenue.
woocommerce.stackImpact: For your stack: hosting is crucial (Kinsta, WP Engine, or a specialized WooCommerce host, not generic shared hosting). Plugin discipline: WooCommerce Subscriptions, WooCommerce Memberships, a payment plugin, a tax plugin. On top of that, switch ALL caching plugins OFF on /cart, /checkout, /my-account, otherwise customers see old order details. SEO via Yoast or Rank Math, the same hygiene as content WordPress.
pitfalls: Caching on transactional pages. Customers see the checkout of a previous visitor.
Updating plugins without staging. The site goes down on a conflict, sometimes hours of downtime.
Leaving the default WordPress login on /wp-admin. Brute-force attacks run continuously.
GA4 tracking through a free plugin, often outdated or buggy. Conversions get missed.

youtube-ads.shortDescription: Video advertising on YouTube for reach and conversion.
youtube-ads.description: YouTube Ads is part of the Google ecosystem and offers powerful options for video advertising. From awareness to conversion, video is an increasingly important part of the marketing mix.
youtube-ads.useCase: Brand awareness and retargeting through video ads.
youtube-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI sets up YouTube campaigns inside your Google Ads account and makes sure view-through conversions and audiences are measured correctly and reused across your other channels.
problemsSolved: No insight into the contribution of video to conversions
YouTube audiences are not reused across other channels
youtube-ads.stevinAngle: YouTube Ads is not a standalone channel but part of your Google Ads account, and that is immediately both its strength and its weakness. The targeting and reach are strong, and audiences are directly reusable within Google. But video measures differently from search: someone sees your ad and buys days later through another channel, and by default that contribution falls between the cracks. We see advertisers stall on this: the view-through conversions are not measured well, so on paper video seems to produce little, and the audiences you build with video are left sitting instead of coming back in search and display. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your Google stack, reads the campaign and conversion data through the API and flags where the measurement leaks or where a built audience stays unused. A person sees the advice first, then the change goes live.
youtube-ads.stackImpact: YouTube Ads runs inside Google Ads, so you do not add a separate platform, but you do share the measurement logic with search and that is where it goes wrong. You need a correct measurement setup that keeps view-through separate, otherwise the contribution of video disappears into the figures of your other channels. The connection runs through the Google API. The real question is whether the audiences you build with video also come back in search and display, because otherwise you are paying for reach that you then throw away.
pitfalls: Not measuring view-through separately, so video seems to produce nothing on paper.
Holding video to the same KPI as search, which steers the channel into the ground.
Not reusing built video audiences in search and display, so you throw reach away.
Assuming a conversion inside Google is automatically attached to the right channel.
